dinkum-3.meaning: All facts kept: age, Instagram, cancer and lung issues, undated death, "Sugar Magnolia", birth name and date, Colorado and Barlow, Garcia, the band list, "Truckin'" and the 1997 Library of Congress listing, Tamalpais Research Institute, Sweetwater Music Hall. "a fixture at every Grateful Dead gig" slightly overstates "a staple".
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "American muso", "the family broke the news on Instagram", "played in a fair few other groups", "He'd kept his hand in on the Bay Area music scene".
dinkum-3.authenticity: Sounds like Australian news copy: "a stint at school in Colorado", "they had a crack at everything from country rock to jam band". Dates in Australian order ("16 October 1947").
dinkum-3.register: Level 3 as asked: news register with a steady Aussie flavour, no swearing (allowed up to vulgarity 1).
dinkum-3.tone: Respectful obituary tone throughout: "has died surrounded by loved ones, his family announced on Saturday".
dinkum-3.flow: Reads cleanly: "Weir picked up the guitar at 13 and found his way into the local bluegrass scene".
dinkum-3.variety: Varied ("muso", "gig", "a fair few", "had a crack at", "kept his hand in"), with "muso" used twice.

engine.meaning: The text is the original almost word for word, but "making various groups with bloke Grateful Dead alumni" and "All groups featured bloke Grateful Dead collaborators" turn "fellow" into nonsense.
engine.sense: "bloke" replaces "fellow" in the sense of "fellow member", the wrong sense both times; "American muso" is the only other change and fits.
engine.authenticity: Not Australian beyond one word, and "bloke Grateful Dead alumni" is something no Australian would write; US date order kept ("October 16, 1947").
engine.register: Essentially untranslated: "The announcement did not specify the date of Weir's death."
engine.tone: The solemn tone of the original is mostly intact, as the text is unchanged, though "bloke Grateful Dead alumni" jars.
engine.flow: "making various groups with bloke Grateful Dead alumni" is ungrammatical; otherwise the original's prose.
engine.essence: The original, barely touched, with two garbled phrases.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every fact kept, with Barlow as "future Grateful Dead member John Perry Barlow" and the full band list; "took the lead on a few tracks" for "several" is fine.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "his old Grateful Dead mates", "a fixture at Grateful Dead gigs", "they covered the lot", "He'd kept his hand in".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural Australian news voice: "From the 1970s he also had a crack at a solo career"; Australian date order.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Respectful: "announced he'd died with his loved ones around him".
yarn-dinkum.variety: Good range ("muso", "mates", "gigs", "had a crack at", "covered the lot", "kept his hand in"), "muso" twice.

yarn-troppo.meaning: All facts are present, but several additions colour or extend them: "Couldn't keep him off a stage.", "Not bad going for a backup singer.", "Good innings, Bobby.", "which they played at just about every Grateful Dead gig going"; "Garcia and Weir shook on starting their own group" adds a handshake; "it was underlying lung issues that got him in the end" is close.
yarn-troppo.sense: Mostly apt ("knocking together one group after another", "plucking away on a banjo"), though "Not bad going for a backup singer" casts him as merely a backup singer, which strains the original's point.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Natural Australian ("Good innings", "the American psychedelic rock outfit"), with a few lines that sound written for effect.
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 3, closer to a yarn: "Sad news out of the States on Saturday", "Couldn't keep him off a stage.", "Good innings, Bobby." No swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: Warm, but the quips ("Not bad going for a backup singer.") lighten an obituary; "Good innings, Bobby." is affectionate.
yarn-troppo.flow: Lively, but "Decades of rhythm guitar and singing for the band, and from the 1970s he was off having a go" is a loose join.
yarn-troppo.variety: Most varied: "outfit", "knocking together", "shook on", "had a crack at", "stepped up", "into his politics", "Good innings".
yarn-troppo.essence: Still the obituary, but with a eulogising voice laid over the news report.

unharnessed.meaning: All facts kept, in order ("a song the Library of Congress named a national treasure in 1997").
unharnessed.sense: Mostly fits, but "a regular at Grateful Dead gigs" for a song strains ("regular" is used of people).
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural, but US date order left in ("On December 31, 1965", "October 16, 1947").
unharnessed.register: A touch light for level 3: "muso", "had a crack at", "a whole heap", but much is plain news English.
unharnessed.tone: Respectful obituary tone kept: "he'd died surrounded by the people he loved".
unharnessed.variety: Varied enough ("muso", "drifted into", "a whole heap", "getting behind").
